blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the intermediate level, debits and credits are used for layered entries that involve more than two accounts. A single transaction can touch four or five accounts at once: cash, receivables, revenue, VAT payable, and sometimes a discount account, all in the same entry.

The rule still holds — total debits must equal total credits — but the number of moving parts grows. Good accountants develop a routine of sketching the entry on paper first, making sure both sides balance before the numbers go into the system.

What looks like bookkeeping pedantry is actually quality control. Every entry verified by hand in advance catches mistakes that automation would let through, and spares the team the harder work of finding the error three weeks later in the ledger.

items.q: According to the text, what makes an entry "layered"?
options: It only affects cash and revenue
It involves more than two accounts
It is entered by more than one person
It is checked twice by automation
items.why: "layered entries that involve more than two accounts" — várias contas na mesma transação.

items.q: What rule still holds for a layered entry?
options: Only cash accounts may be debited
Total debits must equal total credits
No entry may touch more than five accounts
VAT payable is always credited last
items.why: "total debits must equal total credits" — a regra básica não muda, mesmo com mais contas.

items.q: Why do good accountants sketch the entry on paper first?
options: To show the entry to the client
To make sure both sides balance before keying it in
To keep a paper copy for the auditor
items.why: "making sure both sides balance before the numbers go into the system."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Checking an entry by hand is a waste of an accountant's time
Layered entries carry a higher risk of error
Automation does not catch every mistake
Catching a mistake early is cheaper than fixing it later
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende justamente a verificação manual como controle de qualidade, não como perda de tempo.

items.q: What does "spares the team the harder work of finding the error three weeks later" suggest?
options: The team should work in three-week cycles
Automation should be switched off entirely
Errors found late are far more costly to trace
Ledgers are updated only once a month
items.why: Inferência: procurar um erro escondido no razão semanas depois é muito mais trabalhoso do que preveni-lo na entrada.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry orientando um colega júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, before you touch the keyboard, let's draw this one out on paper. It's a sales entry, but it's a layered one — five accounts, not two — so we go slowly.

The customer bought on credit, so we debit receivables for the full amount they owe us. Then we split the credit side. Part of it is revenue, part of it is VAT payable, because the tax isn't ours to keep — we're collecting it for the government. And we gave them a five percent discount, so that goes into the discount account as a debit.

Now here's the habit I want you to build. Before anything goes into the system, add up the debits, add up the credits, and check they match. If they don't balance on paper, they will not balance in the ledger — and finding the gap later is a miserable afternoon.

I know it feels like pedantry. It isn't. This is quality control. Two minutes with a pencil now spares you three weeks of hunting for one missing figure.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Harry ask the junior to do before touching the keyboard?
options: Draw the entry out on paper
items.why: "before you touch the keyboard, let's draw this one out on paper."

items.q: Why is the VAT credited separately, according to Harry?
options: Because the tax is collected for the government, not kept
Because it increases the company's revenue
Because it is the largest part of the sale
items.why: "the tax isn't ours to keep — we're collecting it for the government."

items.q: How is the five percent discount recorded in this entry?
options: As a debit to the discount account
As a credit to VAT payable
items.why: "we gave them a five percent discount, so that goes into the discount account as a debit."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "if they don't balance on paper, they will not balance in the ledger"?
options: An error caught before keying is an error avoided in the books
The paper copy is the only official record
The system will automatically fix any imbalance
The ledger should always be filled in by hand
items.why: Inferência: verificar no papel primeiro impede que o mesmo desequilíbrio entre no razão.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's attitude toward checking by hand?
options: He does it only when the auditor is present
He sees it as outdated and reluctantly follows it
He treats it as real quality control, not fussiness
He thinks automation makes it unnecessary
items.why: Inferência: "I know it feels like pedantry. It isn't. This is quality control." — ele defende o hábito com convicção.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "This is a layered entry, not a simple two-line one." A layered entry is one that…
items.why: Layered = em camadas: toca várias contas na mesma transação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The customer bought on credit, so we debit ___ for the amount they still owe us."
items.why: Receivables = contas a receber: o que o cliente ainda deve à empresa.

items.q: "VAT payable sits on the credit side because the tax isn't ours to keep." VAT payable is…
options: a discount given to the customer
tax collected that the company owes to the government
items.why: VAT payable = IVA a pagar: imposto que a empresa recolhe e deve repassar ao governo.

items.q: "With five accounts in one transaction, there are a lot of moving parts." Moving parts here means…
options: the different elements that must all be handled correctly
items.why: Moving parts = partes móveis: os vários elementos que precisam funcionar juntos.

items.q: "Verifying every entry by hand is a form of quality control." Quality control means…
options: checking work to catch errors before they cause harm
items.why: Quality control = controle de qualidade: checar o trabalho para pegar erros a tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões e revisões de contabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The senior accountant still has to sign off on every layered entry." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's walk through the entry line by line before keying it in." To walk through means to…
options: go over it step by step
items.why: Walk through = percorrer com calma, passo a passo — exatamente o que Harry faz.

items.q: "If the two sides don't balance, we need to track down the missing figure." To track down means to…
items.why: Track down = localizar, caçar até encontrar — o "missing figure" no razão.

items.q: "Automation can let small errors slip through." To slip through means to…
items.why: Slip through = passar despercebido, escapar sem ser pego.

items.q: "Sketching the entry first helps us catch mistakes early." To catch a mistake means to…
items.why: To catch a mistake = pegar/detectar o erro a tempo, antes que cause dano.
